questions.question: What might happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
Both the alcohol and drug effects may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both the alcohol and drug effects may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make the effects of both stronger. For example, drinking one beer while taking a cold medicine could affect you like you drank several beers.

questions.question: What should you do about traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: Always obey them.
They are just suggestions.
Obey them only when other cars are around.
Obey them only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow. They tell drivers about road conditions and help guide them safely. You must always obey them.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need a longer distance to stop than small vehicles.
Need less time to pass going downhill than small vehicles.
Have a tighter turning radius than small vehicles.
Need less time to pass going uphill than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need a longer distance to stop than small vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.
The road ahead curves left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn you about upcoming hazards. This sign warns that the road curves to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: What does alcohol cause?

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower judgment.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Take turns slower than normal.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.explanation: Slippery roads are especially dangerous in turns and curves. Drive through them more slowly than you normally would.

questions.question: You missed your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or make sudden lane changes on the highway. Do not cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning allowed.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You start to feel tired while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drink some coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Driving tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: A sudden weather change means you need to change how you drive.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you during bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Sudden weather changes require you to adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain and fog. Pay special attention to vehicles behind you—they may be going too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle and move it off the road if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or there is more than $1,000 in property damage.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway with multiple lanes, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: An intersection has no signs or lights. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection with no signals at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right of way. Wait for that vehicle to pass safely before you go.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways. Cross only if it is safe.
Cross as fast as possible when a train is coming.
Quickly drive under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways. Cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Listen and look in both directions for a train before you cross. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: You should always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you are doing and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is something blocking the road.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
Two lanes are merging ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road curves sharply in the direction of the arrow. In this case, it curves left. You may see several of these signs placed along a curve.

questions.question: You should not pass another vehicle:

options.text: On a hill or around a curve.
When a school bus has its red lights flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass if a car is coming toward you, your view is blocked by a curve or hill, you are at an intersection, near a railroad crossing or bridge, or in a no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What happens if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine weakens the alcohol's effects.
The alcohol helps the medicine work better.
The combination can make both drugs stronger and more dangerous.
There is no interaction because they are different substances.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can make both drugs stronger and more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol while taking medicine can increase the effects of both. For example, one drink with a cold medicine could affect you as much as several drinks without the medicine.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Driving at night is harder because you cannot see as well. Take these steps to stay safe in the dark for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: If stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of vehicle registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You are required to have all three documents in your vehicle while driving.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at an exit you almost missed. If you pass your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: What can happen when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: Decrease the effects of the drugs and alcohol.
Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
Help cure your illness.
Improve your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the effects of both the drugs and alcohol.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can increase the effects of both. It is unsafe to drive after using either alcohol or drugs alone. It is even more dangerous when you combine them.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow the laws that would be in place if the area was not under construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the flagger.
questions.explanation: Obey a flagger's directions in construction zones. Be ready to slow down and be careful. Not following a flagger is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: You had a bad experience at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
Stop at your favorite bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are angry or upset, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while angry or distracted is poor judgment and very dangerous to you and others on the road.
